prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1431; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for side impact collision at signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a third-party vehicle entering from cross street. Police report requested. Initial liability appears to favor insured based on witness statement and signal phase data. Claimant reports back strain. Claimant is represented by counsel; all further contact to go through attorney's office.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant's attorney's office to confirm representation and receive preliminary medical information. Attorney indicates client was evaluated at urgent care following the collision and diagnosed with lumbar strain. Requested copies of all treatment records and itemized bills. Medical authorization forms sent to counsel for signature.

Entry 3: Reviewed photos submitted by insured showing damage to driver side door, B-pillar, and rear quarter panel. Estimate from preferred body shop pending. Vehicle is drivable but has been moved to storage pending inspection. Scheduled field appraisal for next available slot.

Entry 4: Received signed medical authorization from claimant's counsel. Records from urgent care reviewed; notes document muscle spasm in lower back, prescribed muscle relaxants and physical therapy referral. No imaging performed. Claimant has not yet started physical therapy per counsel. Will follow up for updated status before evaluating bodily injury exposure.

Entry 5: Attorney's office sent demand package requesting settlement for bodily injury and property damage. Demand is under review; medical bills and wage documentation still outstanding. Referred file to supervisor for reserve review and possible early evaluation. Diary set for follow-up with counsel in two weeks.
